title: How to Get More HVAC Leads (Without Overpaying for Shared Ones)

short: The HVAC lead playbook, ranked by cost per booked job: Google Local Service Ads for paid demand (~$168), then the channels you own — Google Business Profile, reviews, referrals — plus answering in minutes.
statLabel: Cost per booked HVAC job via Google Local Service Ads — the strongest paid channel

body.h2: Start with Google Local Service Ads
body.answer: Pay per lead, exclusive-ish, top of the page.
body.html: For HVAC, Google Local Service Ads are the strongest paid channel — ~$168 per booked job, calls come to you (not a pack of 12), and the Google-screened badge builds trust. You pay per lead, and bad leads are disputable.

body.answer: The map pack is where HVAC gets picked.
body.html: Complete every field, post weekly, and build reviews relentlessly — competitive HVAC markets take ~519 to top (BrightLocal 2026) and 91% won't consider under 4 stars. These leads are exclusive and cost nothing per lead.

body.answer: Speed + referrals are the cheapest jobs you'll book.
body.html: Respond in 5 minutes (up to 100x more likely to connect — MIT Sloan 2026), and ask every happy customer for a referral at the peak moment. Owned demand doesn't vanish when you stop paying.

faq.q: What's the best way to get HVAC leads?
faq.a: Google Local Service Ads for paid demand (~$168 per booked job), plus owned channels — a complete Google Business Profile, steady reviews, and referrals — which produce exclusive leads over time.

faq.q: Are Angi leads good for HVAC?
faq.a: Usually expensive per booked job (~$542) because leads are shared with up to 12 pros. Google LSA (~$168) and owned channels are cheaper per job.

faq.q: How fast should I respond to HVAC leads?
faq.a: Within 5 minutes — up to 100x more likely to connect than 30 minutes (MIT Sloan 2026), and 78% of homeowners hire the first responder (Lead Connect 2026).
